presentation: Chaptered implementation/evidence guide, not continuous live screen recording
voice: Windows System.Speech synthetic narration; no person impersonated

scenes.title: 01 / Prepare the assigned native IBM environment
scenes.narration: Provision the assigned LinuxONE Community Cloud VM and complete both organizer-assigned labs before original project work. Our host is RHEL nine point eight and uses Podman with the supplied native s390x image. Preserve persistent notebook storage. The private key stays outside the project. This guide is chaptered evidence and reproducible commands, not a continuous provisioning recording.

scenes.title: 02 / Open the actual IBM VM
scenes.narration: The participant requested public port three eight eight eight eight. An HTTP visit redirects to HTTPS on that same port. Verify the certificate fingerprint manually, then enter the existing Jupyter token. The dashboard uses a different token. The private Jupyter backend is now loopback port three eight eight eight nine. SSH access is another route to the same IBM VM.

scenes.title: 03 / Understand the data and source
scenes.narration: Read SUMMARY and the data card. Hospital-service windows are generated by our original controlled simulator. The separate measured-service CSV contains actual request timings and process counters. The feature module shares twenty-six current and historical inputs between fitting and live inference. Scenario, seed, onset and future outcomes are excluded from the predictors. The model, runtime, API and explanation code are inspectable.

scenes.title: 04 / Train and freeze through Jupyter
scenes.narration: Notebook zero six performs the current fitting, validation selection and first fresh evaluation. Two hundred forty training runs, sixty calibration runs and one hundred twenty validation runs remain separate. The model and protocol hashes are frozen before the one hundred eighty final runs are generated. Notebook zero one reviews those unchanged artifacts. Rerunning the same seeds is reproduction, not another independent test.

scenes.title: 05 / Explain the actual operational policy
scenes.narration: Two logistic and three boosted-tree candidates compete on a declared notification objective. Standardized logistic regression with C equal to zero point one was selected. The first threshold warning is never filtered by low model confidence. Only persistent repeats need the selected learned-risk confirmation. Observed latency or error breach bypasses filtering. Independent model paging is disabled. This is a notification-quality contribution, not a claim of earlier detection on every event.

scenes.title: 06 / Verify the lifecycle correction
scenes.narration: The permanent latch could suppress a qualifying later warning. Shared bounded rechecks now apply to every comparator. The previously missed development case retains its fifty-one-second threshold warning. The final native suite passed 43 tests. Offline and live alert policies share the same source. Missing data resets warmup; failures enter an explicit static fallback. The corrected baseline also benefits, so cross-version recall changes cannot be attributed to ML.

scenes.title: 07 / Read the fresh paired comparison
scenes.narration: On 180 predeclared fresh synthetic runs, both methods warned early for 130 of 135 service incidents. Precision was 45.3 percent versus 43.5 percent. Unmatched notifications fell from 174 to 162. Median early lead stayed 11 seconds, with 1 missed incident each. This is a modest within-simulator improvement, not universal superiority. Whole-run paired resampling retains dependent services together. The rejected version four trial remains published because filtering initial warnings traded recall for precision. No final-test threshold changes were made.

scenes.title: 08 / Inspect actual measurements and Toolkit limits
scenes.narration: Notebook zero four collects original request timings and process counters from a bounded computation service on LinuxONE. It fits a separate baseline novelty detector and retains recovery false alerts. Notebook zero five checks a separate Random Forest ONNX candidate. IBM Toolkit deployment guidance was applied, but entitled Toolkit container execution and hardware acceleration are not claimed. These experiments do not replace the frozen main detector.

scenes.title: 09 / Deploy and verify on LinuxONE
scenes.narration: The deployment script builds a native application container before replacing the named app. It preserves the state volume and a stopped rollback container. Non-root identity, read-only root, dropped capabilities and resource limits are verified. The application stores a local audit chain. Restart checks retain its prefix; this is persistence, not high availability. Private tokens are read internally and excluded from exported evidence.

scenes.title: 10 / Demonstrate the decision workflow
scenes.narration: Choose database connection pressure and four-times replay in the deployed dashboard. Select the first database incident, inspect its retained evidence and request local Granite wording. Preview the allowed simulator response. In the verified current example, modeled urgent-results successes increase by 309, with 1175 optional requests deferred. External data requires its own session; paired simulator previews are disabled there.

scenes.title: 11 / Review and submit
scenes.narration: Review the latest PDF, SUMMARY, model and data cards, resource credits and speaker notes. Prior screenshots and experiments remain clearly labeled history. Read the current frozen report instead of repeating an old model headline. Upload the reviewed short video to an accessible YouTube or Vimeo URL, confirm the mandatory-lab mapping and submit the event portal manually. The longer guide is supporting material.
